track: Fact-check: zero- and low-install ways to deliver the world on the Mac, and giving the agents a GPU

checks.claim: Godot can export and ad-hoc sign a macOS .app from Linux with no Apple Developer account. Notarisation cannot use an ad-hoc signature. An app fetched with curl is not quarantined, so Gatekeeper does not block it; a browser download needs xattr or Open Anyway.
checks.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot/4.7.2-stable/platform/macos/export/export_plugin.cpp (line 513 makes 'Built-in (ad-hoc only)' the default off macOS; line 128 has 'Notarization with an ad-hoc signature is not supported.'); https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/666452 (Apple DTS: 'Most Unix-y tools don't quarantine their downloads, including curl and scp' and 'Gatekeeper usually only kicks in [if] the app is quarantined')
checks.correction: One caveat the report leaves out. If the project uses any GDExtension, such as Terrain3D (listed as optional in ENGINE_SELECTION) or custom C++ for LiDAR streaming, two things follow. First, Godot's docs say an ad-hoc-signed export then needs the 'Disable Library Validation' entitlement (exporting_for_macos.rst line 169). Second, the macOS .dylib must be built. That is awkward from Linux (osxcross needs Apple's SDK), so the free macOS runner would be the practical builder.

checks.claim: The Mac holds a single arm64 app with 82.9 MB of engine for 4.7.2, 'arm64 is thinned by Godot's built-in lipo', about 90–95 MB for 4.8-dev6, so the two M0 apps total about 0.2 GB.
checks.source: My own range-read of the official templates on 23 Sep 2026. 4.7.2 macos.zip contains only godot_macos_release.universal (170,132,160 B; arm64 slice 82,920,128 B) and godot_macos_debug.universal. 4.8-dev6 macos.zip contains only godot_macos_release.universal (232,303,712 B; arm64 slice 113.6 MB; x86_64 slice 118.7 MB). export_plugin.cpp 4.7.2 line 1670 builds the file name as 'godot_macos_release.' + architecture, and line 2057 raises 'Requested template binary "%s" not found'. Line 478 marks the architecture option PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE, so it is hidden in the export dialog. The only LipO use in the plugin is is_lipo() at line 1596. exporting_for_macos.rst line 12: 'apps exported with the official export templates are exported as a single "Universal 2" binary'.
checks.correction: The 82.9 MB arm64 slice size is correct, but Godot does not thin the binary on export. With official templates the only working setting is universal. Choosing arm64 looks for a godot_macos_release.arm64 file that is not in the template zip, and the export fails. A default export therefore carries 170.1 MB (4.7.2) and 232.3 MB (4.8-dev6), about 0.40 GB for the M0 pair. The report's 0.2 GB (82.9 + 113.6 = 196.5 MB) is reachable only if agents strip the Intel half after export with llvm-lipo and re-sign with rcodesign; that path is untested. The 4.8-dev6 arm64 slice is 113.6 MB, not 90–95 MB. The verdict still holds, because 0.4 GB is still light.

checks.claim: The Linux export differs from the Mac build in two ways. (a) Metal shaders cannot be pre-compiled ('baked') on Linux, so the first launch stutters. (b) An arm64 export ships ETC2/ASTC textures, while the cloud renders use S3TC/BPTC.
checks.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-docs/master/tutorials/performance/pipeline_compilations.rst: 'The editor running on Linux can export shaders for Vulkan only'; baking is 'not supported when exporting ... using the --headless' flag. export_plugin.cpp get_preset_features, lines 62–69.
checks.correction: (a) is confirmed. (b) mostly falls away. As the previous check shows, official templates only allow the universal architecture, and universal exports pick S3TC/BPTC. That is the same format the Linux (lavapipe) renders use, and the M2 supports BC formats. The ETC2/ASTC switch only happens with a custom arm64 template. One omission: the owner's repo is public (checked through the session's repo list), so a free macOS runner could run a macOS editor export to bake Metal. That is untested, because Godot's Metal driver crashed on the runner's virtual GPU before (next check).

checks.claim: Free GitHub macOS runners give real Metal, but Godot's Metal renderer crashes on their Apple5 virtual GPU, so they only suit the three.js path.
checks.source: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101773 (closed; Apple Paravirtual device Apple5; 'newArgumentEncoderWithLayout: unrecognized selector'); https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101873 (closed as duplicate; reproduced in 4.4-beta1, not in 4.3); https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99820 (adds Metal shaders without argument buffers for Apple4-class GPUs); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/data/reusables/actions/supported-github-runners.md (free and unlimited on public repos)
checks.correction: The crash evidence is from a 4.4 beta. The issue is now closed, and Godot has since gained a Metal path that skips argument buffers (the feature that crashed), so 4.7/4.8 might work. 'Probably not for Godot' overstates what we know; one free workflow run would settle it. The report assumed the free tier applies without checking; the repo andrekaljevic/Aokigahara is public, so it does.

checks.claim: The browser is the only true zero-install route (Safari on macOS 26+). The M2 Air gets macOS 27.
checks.source: https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/wiki/Implementation-Status (Safari: 'In macOS Tahoe 26 ... WebGPU is supported and enabled by default'; Firefox 145 on macOS 26+, 147 on all versions); https://support.apple.com/en-us/127255 via search snippet (macOS 27 supports 'MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)')
checks.correction: The WebGPU and macOS 27 facts are right. 'Only true zero-install route' contradicts the report's own mac_footprint, which puts browser WebRTC streaming at 0 MB. A browser stream (for example Unreal's Pixel Streaming) is equally zero-install, and it is the only route whose fidelity is not capped by the M2. That bears directly on whether Godot is the highest-yield choice, and the report under-weights it.

checks.claim: Godot's web export is WebGL2/Compatibility only and loses SDFGI, SSIL, SSR, VoxelGI, volumetric fog, TAA, FSR2 and compute shaders, and renders RGBA8 LDR. So drop it.
checks.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-docs/master/tutorials/rendering/renderers.rst (feature tables; the Compatibility renderer is the one the web platform uses)
checks.correction: It is worse than stated. The same table shows Compatibility also lacks decals, FXAA, SMAA, depth of field and debanding. It also uses '24-bit [depth] without reverse Z', which risks depth artefacts (z-fighting) over a 5 km draw distance. Dropping it is correct.

checks.claim: GPU prices and routes. A full GPU VM runs 'roughly £0.33–0.65/h', AWS g6.xlarge (L4) is $0.8048/h in us-east-1, and London is 'probably dearer'. Prefer a full VM to RunPod, because Vulkan is often missing in RunPod containers. First set-up takes 1–3 hours.
checks.source: AWS's own price files, published 21 Sep 2026: https://b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/ec2/USD/current/ec2-ondemand-without-sec-sel/EU%20(London)/Linux/index.json and the US East (N. Virginia) equivalent. https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-on-demand-instance-vcpu-increase and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/instancetypes/ec2-instance-quotas.html (new accounts get a 0-vCPU quota for G instances). https://github.com/SkyeShark/eidoverse-video/issues/5 (11 Sep 2026: NVIDIA Vulkan works on a RunPod RTX 4090 pod after 'apt install libegl1 libgl1 libgles2').
checks.correction: us-east-1 at $0.8048/h is confirmed. In London (eu-west-2), g6.xlarge (L4) is $1.0216/h (about £0.77) and g4dn.xlarge (T4) is $0.615/h (about £0.46). The cheapest UK full VM with an L4 is therefore about £0.77/h, above the stated range. The 20 GPU-hour AWS scenario becomes about £15, plus disk storage billed while stopped. New AWS accounts start with a 0-vCPU G-instance quota, and raising it needs a support request, so '1–3 hours' is optimistic on AWS. The RunPod Vulkan problem is fixable in a stock pod with three packages. That makes 'prefer a full VM' over-cautious, though Godot still needs an X server on the NVIDIA driver to draw. The RunPod prices themselves (L4 $0.44, A4000 $0.17) are unverifiable: runpod.io is blocked by the proxy, and search results say Community Cloud rates float and it no longer takes new hosts.

checks.claim: Hetzner GEX44 costs €184 a month (reportedly €234 from August 2026) plus a €79 set-up fee.
checks.source: Search snippets only; hetzner.com and docs.hetzner.com are blocked by the proxy. https://www.whtop.com/plans/hetzner.com/128304 (€184 + €79, the 2024 launch price); Fudzilla and Hetzner pressroom snippets (€182.30 to €212.30 in Feb 2026); another snippet gives '€234/month plus €114 setup'.
checks.correction: The €79 set-up fee is probably out of date. Hetzner raised set-up fees in 2026, and one snippet gives €114. Treat the figure as €212–234 a month plus about €79–114 set-up until Hetzner's own page can be read.

checks.claim: GitHub GPU and large runners. A T4 runner is $0.052/min (about £2.35/h) and a macOS M2 Pro runner $0.102/min. Both need a GitHub Team or Enterprise Cloud organisation; Team is $4 per user per month for the first 12 months.
checks.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing.md (linux_4_core_gpu $0.052, macos_xl $0.102); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/data/reusables/actions/larger-runner-permissions.md; https://github.com/pricing ('$4 USD per user/month for the first 12 months'); larger-runners.md (T4, 28 GB RAM, 16 GB VRAM, 176 GB SSD, NVIDIA GPU-Optimized VMI partner image)

checks.claim: Claude Code on the agents' side. Self-hosted environments need Team or Enterprise. Remote Control works on Pro and Max. Cross-session messaging can bring the Mac's benchmark JSON back to the cloud session; whether the cloud session can start that exchange is less clear. Team is $25 per seat per month ($20 annually) with a 2-seat minimum and about 1.25× Pro usage.
checks.source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/self-hosted-environments ('public beta on Team and Enterprise plans and are off by default'); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control ('available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported'); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging (from v2.1.225 a Remote Control session can start a conversation with another machine; messages to cloud sessions go 'straight to the cloud session'); this cloud session's own ListAgents tool description ('a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet'); https://claude.com/pricing (Team $25 monthly / $20 annually, 'For teams of 2 to 150')
checks.correction: The plan limits and Team prices are confirmed. The seat multiplier is not: the pricing page says only 'more usage than Pro', so 1.25× is unverified. On messaging, the Mac session (if connected via Remote Control) can push results to the cloud session. The cloud agents cannot currently message the Mac, so they cannot ask it to run a benchmark. The owner, or the owner driving the Mac session from claude.ai/code, has to start each Mac bench.

checks.claim: Web hosting and browser storage. GitHub Pages is capped at 1 GB. Cloudflare R2 includes 10 GB-month free, then $0.015 per GB-month, with free egress. Chromium allows 60% of disk per origin; WebKit allows about 60% per origin and 80% overall. Safari deletes script-written data after 7 days without user interaction.

omissions: Streaming is zero-install too. A browser WebRTC client (for example UE Pixel Streaming) needs 0 MB on the Mac, and it is the only route that can reach photoreal. The report calls the browser 'the only true zero-install route', which contradicts its own footprint table. This is the most decision-relevant gap for the owner's question.

Data-transfer charges on streaming. After the first 100 GB a month, AWS charges about $0.09/GB for data sent out (search snippet: egresscost.com/aws/data-transfer-pricing). A 1080p60 stream at 20–30 Mbps is about 9–13 GB/hour, so roughly $0.8–1.2/hour of egress, about as much as the L4 instance itself. Providers with free or bundled egress change the ranking.
AWS start-up friction. New accounts have a 0-vCPU G-instance quota and must request an increase. London rates are about 27% above us-east-1. Disk storage is billed while the instance is stopped.

Flat-rate cloud PCs are not considered. Shadow offers a Windows PC with an RTX-class GPU, macOS and browser clients, and plans of $29.99–54.99 a month in the US (Aug 2026), with a Lite tier from €19.49 (search snippets; GBP prices, UK data centre and terms of use unverified). One such box could host UE5 or Godot for streaming and also give the agents a GPU through Claude Code Remote Control on Windows. For regular use it may cost less than hourly VMs.
Official Godot macOS templates are universal-only. Each exported app is 170 MB (4.7.2) or 232 MB (4.8-dev6) unless agents strip the Intel half and re-sign it themselves.

Native code on the Mac. Any GDExtension (Terrain3D, custom LiDAR streaming code) needs macOS dylibs built on a Mac, which the free public-repo macOS runner can do, plus the 'Disable Library Validation' entitlement for ad-hoc signing.
Publishing licence. The repo is public, so free macOS runners apply. Publishing a world pack (GitHub, R2) may also be limited by the LiDAR or photogrammetry source licence (not checked).

OS update space. Getting Safari WebGPU on macOS 26/27 needs an OS update, and its temporary disk space on a 256 GB Air is unverified. Chrome or Firefox 147+ avoid the update but are installs of their own.
overall:
The report is mostly accurate and well sourced. The checks on signing, quarantine, shader baking, WebGPU, the Compatibility renderer's gaps, GitHub runner pricing, Claude plan gating, R2/Pages and browser storage all held up against primary sources.

Four problems need fixing:
1. **Godot does not thin exports to arm64.** Official templates ship only universal binaries, so a default exported app is 170 MB (4.7.2) or 232 MB (4.8-dev6). The M0 pair is about 0.4 GB unless agents strip it manually. The 4.8-dev6 arm64 slice is 113.6 MB, not 90–95 MB. The texture-format 'cost' largely disappears.
2. **UK GPU VM prices are optimistic.** London L4 is $1.02/h (about £0.77), T4 $0.615/h. New AWS accounts start with a 0-vCPU GPU quota, and streaming egress is omitted.
3. **The RunPod Vulkan problem is fixable** with three packages, so 'prefer a VM' is over-cautious. RunPod and Hetzner prices remain unverified.
4. **The Mac-to-cloud hand-off only runs one way.** The Mac session can send results to the cloud agents, but they cannot currently message the Mac.

None of this overturns the report's narrow conclusion that Godot survives the 'nothing heavy on the Mac' rule: 0.4 GB is still light. But the report under-weights the one route that answers the owner's photoreal brief. Streaming from a cloud GPU is also zero-install through the browser and is not capped by the M2; its real costs are GPU hours plus egress. The report also skips flat-rate cloud PCs, and it leaves UE5 on a cloud GPU to the streaming track. So the report does not show that Godot is the highest-yield choice for photorealism, only that it is viable without a heavy install. UE5 in the cloud still needs the owner's explicit OK.
